result:
I planned the test suite for `001-quickflow`. Nothing was run in this step, since the planning step only writes the checklists.

All six user stories (US1–US6) are marked done in both the backend and frontend loops, so every story is in the suite and none is left out as not ready.

I wrote nine checklists in `loops/testing/outputs/001-quickflow/suite/`, in the order they depend on each other:

| Test phase | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `test-phase-01` | **API contract:** all 39 endpoints in the generated API spec, called with curl. Checks status codes and response formats, and that create/update/delete/filter calls finish in under 500 ms. |
| `test-phase-02` … `07` | **One phase per story, US1 to US6** (tasks, habits, learning, plans, dashboard, settings). Each checks that story's rules through the API first, then the same behaviour in the browser with Playwright. |
| `test-phase-E2E` | **The end-to-end flow from the PRD, step by step as it lists it.** It includes waiting in real time for a plan to start (checking the in-app notice) and reading the countdown twice to see it go down. |
| `test-phase-regression` | **Every earlier per-phase check again** (19 test plans), plus the unit tests with domain coverage of at least 80%. |

The generated API spec only lists success codes, so I took the expected 400/404/409 codes from the planning contract (`specs/001-quickflow-backend/contracts/openapi.yaml`). The browser checks use the element IDs listed in `ui-contract.md`.

I set `loops/testing/state/001-quickflow/suite.json` to `running`, with all nine phases `planned` at attempt 1, and added one line to `progress.md`. Next, the runner runs `test-phase-01`.
